topic: Which capital is split into Buda and Pest? (Budapest)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

britannica_budapest.title: Budapest
britannica_budapest.notes: divided by the Danube into Buda (west: hills, higher terraces) and Pest (east: flat sandy plain); eight bridges incl. the Széchenyi Chain Bridge; banks of the Danube = UNESCO site

wiki_budapest.title: Budapest
wiki_budapest.notes: Buda, Óbuda and Pest officially unified in 1873 and given the new name Budapest; Chain Bridge opened 1849 as the first permanent bridge across the Danube

wiki_chain_bridge.title: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
wiki_chain_bridge.notes: spans the Danube between Buda (west) and Pest (east); first permanent bridge across the Danube in Hungary; opened 1849

usf_pesth.publisher: University of South Florida — Educational Technology Clearinghouse
usf_pesth.title: The bridge at Pesth
usf_pesth.notes: Pest = eastern flat part; 1849 Chain Bridge; 1873 unification with Óbuda to become Budapest

britannica_danube.title: Danube River
britannica_danube.notes: second-longest river in Europe, about 2,850 km; passes through 10 countries; four national capitals on its banks: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade

wiki_danube.title: Danube
wiki_danube.notes: 2,850 km; connects ten countries; four national capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade

unesco_budapest.title: Budapest, including the Banks of the Danube, the Buda Castle Quarter and Andrássy Avenue
unesco_budapest.notes: World Heritage listing of the Hungarian capital's Danube banks; description: the Danube originally separated two towns — Buda on the right-bank spur and Pest on the left-bank plain

britannica_kosovo.title: Kosovo
britannica_kosovo.notes: self-declared independent country since 2008; Serbia does not recognise its independence; recognised by about 100 UN member states

myths.myth: Budapest has always been one city.
myths.reality: Buda, Óbuda and Pest were separate towns until the 1873 unification.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

landscape.our_gap: The feed says 'Budapest' over skyline footage; nobody draws the river through the city and then pulls out to the four capitals on the same line.
